gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-bassa-v: Plakkaat is heavy bent-straw lettering, its terminals curling almost to touch the stem, while Noto Sans Bassa Vah gapes open. Down a whole page, the dominant midsection keeps each line steady.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-bengali: Strokes like bent straw, with terminals sweeping round to nearly touch the stem, give Plakkaat its heavy character. Noto Sans Bengali then opens every letter mouth, with capitals barely above lowercase, for a smooth read.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-cheroke: The text reads friendly and roomy, with a deep band of letters, short stalks above, and an e gaping at its terminal. Noto Sans Cherokee is the open-mouthed counterweight to Plakkaat's closed, heavy forms.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-deseret: Noto Sans Deseret keeps its apertures open and its lowercase wide-looking, with squat ascenders that stay low. Plakkaat, with its closed bent-straw letters and heavy hand, is at home when big and brief.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-glagoli: Noto Sans Glagolitic reads in an approachable, unfussy way, with open round letters and a sturdy lowercase body. Over pages of text it runs smoothly beside Plakkaat's closed, heavy forms.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-grantha: Noto Sans Grantha reads smoothly, never snagging on a closed-up bowl. Plakkaat is its closed, heavy opposite, and shrunk to a small size its low-contrast bent-straw strokes would lose their punch.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-gujarat: Fat, curled, unmissable: Plakkaat's terminals nearly close, while Noto Sans Gujarati lets its curved strokes stop before turning inward. Its big counters keep a full page of text clean and light.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-gunjala: Plakkaat's strokes look like bent straw, heavy and curled. Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi counters with crayon-mark lowercase strokes and terminals cut back to a wide gap, giving a modern open read.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Plakkaat arrives heavy, with curled terminals almost touching the stem. It hits hardest with closed, heavy shapes, while Noto Sans Hebrew works through a dominant midsection and wide gaps where curves meet stems.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-jp: Plakkaat brings heavy, closed bent-straw letters, while Noto Sans JP sweeps its curves open on a very high x-height. One packs its punch tight, the other lets the line breathe.
